criterion_notes.c1: Examines the household connection gap to public network wastewater systems in four municipalities of Minas Gerais, Brazil (Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirão das Neves, BBCR).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2 because it examines an ex-ante Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) framework as a regulatory governance decision-support tool for the state water and wastewater regulator (ARSAE), discussing statutory mandatory connection rules (Federal Law no. 11445/2007, art. 45; State Law no. 13317/1999, art. 48) and tariff regulation as background. However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2: mandatory connection enforcement and tariff rules are treated only as unanalysed institutional background and post-hoc suggestions, while the four 'regulatory policy options' actually evaluated in the model are generic hypothetical infrastructure-diffusion targets (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0% reductions in non-connected households) appraised via an ex-ante MCDA decision-aid procedure rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing access. Even under the plain reading of Criterion 2, the paper remains excluded because it is an ex-ante hypothetical MCDA simulation with assumed connection targets rather than empirical access outcomes (plain_criterion2_decision = exclude).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary stakeholder preference-elicitation data (a stakeholder focus group, conference panel, and web survey used to construct M-MACBETH value functions and criterion weights) alongside secondary municipal baseline statistics and linear projections, though it contains no empirical evidence of real-world regulatory implementation or observed impacts on household connections.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4 because household connection figures (0; 26,768; 53,537; and 107,074 non-connected households in Table 1) are exogenously assumed hypothetical target reductions (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0% of the baseline gap) used as scenario inputs, while the evaluated outputs are normative stakeholder MCDA attractiveness scores and projected downstream hospital stays, utility revenues/costs, and sludge reductions.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5 for review inclusion because the design is a prospective ex-ante MCDA and cost-benefit decision-support exercise comparing hypothetical future infrastructure-diffusion targets (2016–2023 / 2017–2026); there is no implemented legal/regulatory exposure and no empirically measured household access outcome.

evidence_quotes.quote: Moreover, the gap regarding non-connected households exceeds 365,000 inhabitants.
To overcome this problem, the present paper provides an opportunity to observe an ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) as a policy tool in Brazil.

Nevertheless, the agency can act within the parameters of its rules, mainly through the design of tariff mechanisms that are capable of promoting the desired outcomes that highlight the importance of the proposed analysis.
A conference panel and a web survey were used to obtain value functions and weights of the criteria.

Results show that the most indicated political decision is intermediate infrastructure diffusion (A2). To promote a 75% reduction of non-connected households until the year 2023, a BRL 33 million expenditure is expected.

For all hypothetical alternatives, the authors considered that the deployment cycle will occur within seven years (2016 to 2023). To implement the MCDA modeling method, the core of the RIA framework, some criteria were required.
This ex ante analysis allows a critical assessment of the household connection gap, although there is clear room for ex post analysis.

raw_response.exposure: Four hypothetical ex-ante policy targets for reducing the household wastewater connection gap (2016–2023 / 2017–2026): strong infrastructure diffusion (A1, 100%), advanced infrastructure diffusion (A2, 75%), intermediate infrastructure diffusion (A3, 50%), and do nothing (A4, 0%)
raw_response.outcome: Multi-criteria attractiveness scores (M-MACBETH RPO scores) and ex-ante cost-benefit rankings across assumed non-connected household targets (CSo1), projected hospital stays/year (CSo2), projected utility tariff revenues and capex/opex (CEc1, Infra), and projected sludge removal (CEn1)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Four municipalities in Minas Gerais regulated by ARSAE — Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirão das Neves (BBCR; approximately 3.85 million people with wastewater coverage and >365,000 inhabitants / 107,074 baseline non-connected households) — plus a stakeholder focus group, conference panel, and web survey of ARSAE, academic, and local government participants (exact respondent sample size not reported)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (primary code E03; also fails on c4/c5 and prospective non-evaluative study design E12). Although the paper addresses the household connection gap to public wastewater networks in four Brazilian municipalities regulated by ARSAE (c1 = yes) and mentions mandatory connection statutes (Law no. 11445/2007, art. 45; Law no. 13317/1999, art. 48) and tariff incentives as institutional background, it does not examine a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism governing service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope. Instead, it demonstrates an ex-ante Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) / Multiple Criteria Decision Analysis (M-MACBETH) exercise comparing four hypothetical infrastructure-diffusion targets (100%, 75%, 50%, and 0% reductions in non-connected households). Moreover, even under the plain wording of Criterion 2 (where RIA as a regulatory governance tool would pass c2), the paper is excluded because RIA was not implemented in practice, household connection levels (0; 26,768; 53,537; and 107,074 non-connected households) are exogenously assumed scenario inputs rather than empirically measured access outcomes, and the primary data consist solely of stakeholder preference weights used to rank hypothetical targets and their projected health, revenue, and sludge impacts.
raw_response.study_design: Ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) using multiple criteria decision analysis (MCDA / M-MACBETH) and cost-benefit analysis parameterized via a stakeholder focus group, conference panel, web survey, and linear baseline projections
